details:
**Hiding in the cave (Ama-no-Iwato)**
After her brother Susanoo's rampage, Amaterasu shut herself inside the Heavenly Rock Cave, plunging the world into darkness. The other gods had to devise a way to lure her back out to restore the sun.

**Susanoo throws a flayed horse into her weaving hall**
Susanoo, the storm god, flayed a heavenly piebald horse and threw it through the roof of Amaterasu's sacred weaving hall, causing a weaving maiden to die of fright. This outrage was what made Amaterasu hide in the cave.

**Sacred mirror (Yata no Kagami)**
The gods hung a mirror outside the cave. When Amaterasu peeked out, she saw her own bright reflection and was drawn further out, and the gods quickly blocked the cave behind her. The mirror is said to represent her and is kept at the Ise Shrine.

**Ame-no-Uzume's dance**
The goddess Ame-no-Uzume danced wildly on an overturned tub outside the cave, exposing herself and making the assembled gods roar with laughter. Amaterasu grew curious about the noise and looked out, falling for the trick with the mirror.

**Ninigi and the Three Sacred Treasures**
Amaterasu sent her grandson Ninigi down from heaven to rule Japan, giving him the three imperial regalia: the mirror Yata no Kagami, the jewel Yasakani no Magatama and the sword Kusanagi (the "grass-cutter"). These treasures remain symbols of the emperor's authority.

**Ancestor of the Japanese imperial family**
Through Ninigi, whose great-grandson Jimmu became the legendary first emperor of Japan, the imperial dynasty claims direct descent from Amaterasu.

**Ise Grand Shrine rebuilt every 20 years**
Amaterasu's chief shrine, the Inner Shrine (Naiku) at Ise, is torn down and rebuilt on an adjacent plot every twenty years in a ritual called Shikinen Sengu. It is the most sacred site in Shinto.

**Born from Izanagi's left eye**
When the creator god Izanagi purified himself after visiting the underworld, Amaterasu was born from the washing of his left eye. The moon god Tsukuyomi came from his right eye and Susanoo from his nose; these three are the most important children of Izanagi.

**Contest with Susanoo: sword and jewels**
To test Susanoo's intentions, Amaterasu and her brother held a contest of producing children. She broke his sword into three pieces, chewed them and spat out three goddesses, while he chewed her string of jewels and produced five male gods.

**Sun goddess of Shinto**
Amaterasu Omikami ("Great Divinity Illuminating Heaven") is the sun goddess and ruler of the heavenly realm Takamagahara. She is the most important deity of Shinto, and one of her other names is Ohirume-no-muchi.

**Silkworms and the start of agriculture**
In the Nihon Shoki, after the food goddess Ukemochi was killed, rice, grain and silkworms came from her body. Amaterasu planted the grains in her fields and put the silkworms in her mouth to draw out thread, starting rice farming and silk production.
